purpose: Structured projection of Brew's canonical-runtime drift recovery, reference reuse, and acceptance gates. Navigation state only; current Brew repository/runtime evidence remains authoritative.
authority_rule: Current Brew runtime/source, exact revision, live evidence, CI, and project-owned checkpoints outrank this GPT-K projection. Upstream references challenge implementation design but do not become Brew authority.

nodes.title: One primary reasoning identity, one canonical runtime, bounded delegation
nodes.summary: Brew retains the user-level goal and user relationship; runtime owns canonical policy/execution/evidence boundaries. Bounded subagents, specialist agents, teams, planners, supervisors and workers are valid when they add capability without becoming competing product authorities.

nodes.title: Prevent deterministic semantic interception; preserve useful delegation
nodes.summary: PR #439 head e7e68b86 contains a source-proven active pre-model tool-selection boundary: requestHints() regex scoring restricted the model-visible capability registry and enforced exclusions before reasoning. Later main removes this selector and exposes the governed executable registry directly. Preserve governed subagents/teams/specialists; reject only machine behavior that preempts reasoning or creates conflicting authority.

nodes.title: Preserve useful subagents, teams, specialists, and workers
nodes.summary: Working subagents, specialist agents, teams, planners, supervisors and workers are valid product capabilities when bounded and governed. KEEP/ADAPT/COMBINE before removal; only broken, fake, unreachable, unsafe, obsolete-after-migration, or conflicting-authority implementations are removal candidates.

nodes.title: Canonical conversational turn path
nodes.summary: Supported HTTP chat aliases converge toward the canonical query/runTurn path; this remains the response authority to preserve.

nodes.title: Recover drift and converge on upstream-proven contracts
nodes.summary: Remove only proven conflicting semantic authorities and weaker/fake success contracts. Preserve working capabilities, including useful subagents/teams/workers, and reuse/adapt/combine before replacement.

nodes.title: One model-turn success invariant
nodes.summary: Every active adapter must reject empty assistant output when there is no model tool activity and must preserve provider/runtime failures without fabricating assistant text.

nodes.title: Telegram is transport, not a second agent
nodes.summary: Ordinary natural-language Telegram input must reach the canonical turn exactly once; only explicit runtime/transport commands remain deterministic.

nodes.title: Quarantine duplicate response authorities
nodes.summary: Prove consumers before retaining main-agent/direct-response, response-decision, brew-chat-agent, scenario-router and other stale semantic surfaces.

nodes.title: Canonical Session / Turn / Item lifecycle
nodes.summary: Adopt Codex/OpenHands-style lifecycle separation without creating a second persistence authority.

nodes.title: Canonical capability registry and health
nodes.summary: Extend existing Brew capability ownership using Hermes/LobeHub registry patterns; configured is not equivalent to ready.

nodes.title: Provider-native tool continuation
nodes.summary: Prove model call -> governed tool -> evidence -> provider continuation -> final non-empty response.

nodes.title: Cancellation / restart / resume / exactly-once
nodes.summary: Use explicit identity and runtime events; do not infer recovery or completion from loop termination.

nodes.title: MCP, skills, scheduler, browser/desktop and knowledge expansion
nodes.summary: Recover planned capabilities after canonical response/lifecycle authority is stable; adapt upstream patterns rather than adding parallel managers.

nodes.title: Installed runtime + current-head CI acceptance
nodes.summary: No release claim until installed runtime, live acceptance and current-head CI are proven.

nodes.title: Treat PR #439 as feature source, not merge candidate
nodes.summary: Port only missing evidence/verification/observability capabilities from PR #439 onto current canonical owners. Do not port task-tool-selection semantic prefiltering, scenario-style routing, or other pre-model semantic authority.
